request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export pools (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-pools"`) on the main screen, next to the people and claims export buttons. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The download starts with the header `pool,member,share,cut`, then has one line per member. Pools and members come in the order they were added, a member that is itself a pool is written as `pool:<name>`, and the cut is written as shown on screen (blank when there is none). Values with commas, such as `"Lee, Jo"`, are quoted the same way as in the people export.

When the button is pressed, it fetches the pools from the server again before building the file. Without that, a change made elsewhere, like retiring a person, could leave old cuts in the export. The test checks exactly this: after Ada is retired, her cut drops to 0.00.

This only touched the front end: a new `src/main/frontend/features/export/ExportPools.tsx`, plus one line in `home.slot.tsx` that places the button. No server, database or audit changes were needed, because the existing pools endpoint already returns the names, shares and cuts.
